name: search_files
description:
Search plain-text files by content inside registered source directories, similar to a safe rg/ripgrep query. Matching is literal by default; use regex=true only for intentional Rust regex patterns. Use literal mode for exact text, phrases, identifiers, snippets, and strings containing regex metacharacters such as |, ., *, ?, [, or (. Escape metacharacters such as \| only when regex=true and you need them matched literally. Use this when you need to find text or regex patterns in local files before reading or editing them. For coding/codebase browsing, use this as the default first pass to locate declarations, usages, imports, tests, configuration keys, error text, TODOs, or implementation seams, then follow up with read_file/read_files only for the relevant matched paths or line ranges. In restricted mode, searches are limited to the current registered source scope; allow-all/non-restricted permission modes can search all registered sources, and open mode can search an explicitly supplied absolute local path.

This tool searches file contents, not the indexed knowledge base. Use search_knowledge_base first for evidence retrieval across indexed documents; use search_files when you need source-local text locations, line numbers, or files that may not be indexed yet.

query.description: Text to search for. Treated as exact literal text unless regex=true, so characters such as | are literal by default.

path.description: Optional file or directory path to search. If omitted, searches all directories in the current source scope.

regex.description: Treat query as a Rust regular expression instead of literal text (default false). Do not enable this for exact text; if regex=true and you need a literal |, escape it as \|.

include_globs.description: Optional glob patterns to include, such as *.md or notes/**/*.txt

exclude_globs.description: Optional glob patterns to exclude, such as **/archive/**

max_results.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return (default 50, max 200)

context_lines.description: Number of surrounding lines to include before and after each match (default 0, max 3)

include_hidden.description: Include dotfiles and hidden directories (default false)
